# Riffhouse

> Riffhouse is a free, open-source guitar amp simulator and pedalboard for Windows 10 and 11. It runs on its own or as a VST3 plugin, with 11 amps, 30 pedals, 12 cabinets and 197 tones, and it works through a computer's mic jack with no audio interface.

Current version: 0.1.7, released 2026-11-23. Price: free (0 USD), with no account, no ads and no paid version. Platform: Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit. Licence: AGPL-3.0, open source. Made by Natik Chhabra.

## What it has

- 11 amps, 30 pedals, 12 cabinets and 197 ready tones
- Standalone app and VST3 plugin
- Works through a computer's mic jack, no audio interface needed
- Setup that finds the guitar input and sets levels by itself
- Loads .nam amp captures and cabinet impulse responses
- Tuner, looper, metronome, play along with slow-down, take recorder
- No account, no ads, no paid version
- Open source under the AGPL-3.0 licence

## Questions

### What is Riffhouse?

Riffhouse is a free, open-source guitar amp simulator and pedalboard for Windows 10 and 11. It runs on its own or as a VST3 plugin, with 11 amps, 30 pedals, 12 cabinets and 197 tones.

### Is it really free?

Yes. No price, no account, no ads in the app and no paid tier, now or later. The code is open under the AGPL-3.0 licence. Why it’s free.

### Do I need an audio interface?

No. Plug the guitar into the computer’s mic jack with a 6.35 mm to 3.5 mm adapter or cable. A laptop with one combined headset socket needs a splitter with a separate mic socket. If you own an interface, pick it as your input. Its maker’s ASIO driver is used when it works. How to plug in.

### Will I hear myself late?

The rig itself adds next to nothing. What you feel is your computer’s audio buffer, and setup picks the shortest one that runs clean.

### Does it work in my recording software?

Yes. The installer adds a VST3 plugin of the same rig, for any DAW on Windows that loads VST3. See the DAW guide.

### Can I use my own captures?

Yes. Any .nam file loads as the amp and any impulse response as the cabinet. Drop the file on the window.

### Do the tones copy a famous player?

No. Tones are named for the sound they make, like “Dark Singing Lead” or “Fast Dry Thrash Rhythm”, never for a person, a band or a song. Riffhouse has no tie to any artist, band or equipment maker.

### Is there a Mac or Linux version?

No installer yet. You can build it from source today.

### Something is broken. Where do I say so?

Start with Help and fixes. Still stuck? Settings has report buttons under Help. One opens the GitHub page with a report ready to paste. Tone requests go there too.
